settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.d: The environment variables Combwork leaves out when it runs Claude Code on a connection (its sign-in, its checks, Set Up and its agents), by name: a key, token, request header, server, provider switch or model set on this PC can't stand in for the connection's own. Wrong, a variable Claude Code reads as a login, a header or a server could make a connection run as someone else, or send a key elsewhere.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.e: The field of `claude auth status --json` with the email a connection's folder is signed in as. Wrong, Combwork can't tell who a connection is signed in as, and can't warn when its login changes.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l: The field of `claude auth status --json` that says whether a connection's folder is signed in. Wrong, Combwork can't tell, and its sign-in connections show "Couldn't check".
The field of `claude auth status --json` with when a connection's sign-in expires, shown under its state in Settings → Accounts & Connections (HI-2528). Wrong, no expiry is shown.

The names of the files in a connection's folder that change when Claude Code signs in or out there, as a regular expression. settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o: The field of a connection folder's `.claude.json` that says Claude Code's first-run screens were answered there (read only). Wrong, every Claude Code connection shows "Needs set up" in Settings → Accounts & Connections.

The field of `claude auth status --json` with the organisation's id a connection's folder is signed in to. With the email, it tells two logins apart. Wrong, Combwork can't tell who a connection is signed in as.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.p: The field of `claude auth status --json` with a connection's plan ("max"), shown beside its email in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Wrong, no plan is shown.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.s: How long Combwork gives `claude auth status` to say who a connection's folder is signed in as. Past it, the connection shows "Couldn't check", never signed out.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.t: The field of a folder's entry under `projects` in a connection folder's `.claude.json` that says Claude Code was told to trust that folder (read only). Wrong, every Claude Code connection on in a workspace shows "Needs set up" in Settings → Accounts & Connections.
settings.advanced.claude-code.autoModeSe: Claude Code offers, now and then in auto mode, to read the project, your recent sessions and optionally your shell history and other repositories, to teach auto mode about your environment. Combwork never answers it: the agent waits for you. Off, Combwork's Claude Code agents are started with the offer turned off for that launch (nothing is written to Claude Code's files, and auto mode decides as before); /auto-mode-setup still runs it when you want.
settings.advanced.claude-code.connection: The model names Ollama runs on ollama.com rather than on this PC (its cloud models, such as gpt-oss:120b-cloud), as a regular expression, for an Ollama connection's models typed in rather than read from Ollama (Read Models asks Ollama, which says). Such a connection's sessions aren't free (local). Wrong, a cloud model typed in is counted as free, or a local one as not free.
settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.comma: What Combwork types into Claude Code, then Enter, to end it once its lane has ended and its turn is over, so it exits by itself rather than being killed. Wrong, Claude Code isn't ended by it and is killed after the exit grace.
settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.grace: How long Combwork gives Claude Code to exit by itself after typing its exit command at a lane's end, before killing it. It took {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} when recorded.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know: The hook events Combwork knows Claude Code sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.

The top-level fields Combwork knows Claude Code sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a Claude Code update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.preT: How long Claude Code waits for Combwork's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Combwork doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.time: How long Claude Code waits for Combwork to take one of its hooks (a turn starting or ending, a notification). Combwork answers at once; raise it only if Combwork's log shows hooks timing out on a slow machine.
settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea: A connection's projects folder is a link to Claude Code's own, so Claude Code asked you before each memory it saved there. Each Claude Code agent on a connection is given its project's auto memory folder by its real path: the same folder, so it saves memories without asking, as it does without a connection. Nothing more is allowed, and nothing is written to Claude Code's files. Off, Claude Code asks before each memory on a connection.
Auto memory by its real path on connections
settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.set: The Claude Code setting that names its auto memory folder, which Combwork sets on a connection (Auto memory by its real path on connections) and leaves alone where you set it yourself. Wrong, Claude Code ignores it and asks before each memory on a connection.
settings.advanced.claude-code.mouse.righ: Right-click in a Claude Code pane is Combwork's, as in every pane: it copies the terminal's selection, or pastes. Turned on, Combwork passes right-clicks to Claude Code instead. Claude Code doesn't use the mouse at its prompt, so there a right-click then does nothing: copy and paste with Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V.
settings.advanced.claude-code.outage.con: What a StopFailure hook's message says when Claude Code couldn't reach its API after its retries: with Resume agents after a connection drops on, Combwork waits for the connection and resumes the agent. Wrong, such agents stay stopped.
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.m: Combwork starts Claude Code with --strict-mcp-config, so its sessions get only the MCP servers the workspace gives them. Turned off, the servers in your own Claude Code config and the project's .mcp.json load beside them, as they would outside Combwork (Claude Code may ask you to approve a project's new servers first). The workspace's servers, Combwork's own combwork server among them, win over yours of the same name.
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p: When the Assistant runs on Claude Code, Combwork passes --allowedTools with the Combwork tools its Control settings let it use without asking, so Claude Code doesn't ask before them. Turned off, Claude Code asks before each Combwork tool as its own permission mode says. Control still decides what the Assistant may do either way. Agents' Combwork tools are never pre-approved on Claude Code.

When the Assistant's conversation resumes, Combwork starts Claude Code with --system-prompt-snapshot off, so the Assistant follows its role and Control settings as they are now. Turned off, Combwork leaves the flag out and Claude Code keeps sending the instructions it recorded when the conversation began, until it compacts: a change to the Assistant's settings may not reach it until then. --system-prompt-snapshot in Extra arguments wins either way.
Resume the Assistant with its current instructions
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.s: Combwork starts Claude Code with a status line of its own, which sends Combwork the session's model, context, cost and plan limits for the agent's footer and shows nothing under the input. Turned off, the status line in your Claude Code settings shows again: Combwork's command still reads the status, then runs yours with the same input Claude Code gives it and shows what it prints. With no status line of yours, nothing changes.
Combwork's status line in place of yours
settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cle: Claude Code's Ctrl+U deletes one row of a draft that wraps onto several, so before Combwork types into it, it presses Ctrl+U a key at a time until the input box (Screen: input box) shows empty. This is how long Combwork waits for Claude Code to show each key's effect. Not shown in time, Combwork types nothing and tries again later: too short, and a busy Claude Code makes Combwork put its messages off more often.
Clearing the input: wait for each key
settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cli: What a prompt hook's text starts with when Claude Code starts a turn by itself, such as when a background task ends. Combwork never reports such a turn to the Assistant as your reply. Wrong, a background task's end soon after you pressed Enter in the agent's pane can be reported as your reply.
Prompt hook: Claude Code's own turn
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.atte: The field of that entry with which try it is (1, 2…). Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.chec: How long a working Claude Code session has to go without a hook before Combwork looks at the end of its transcript for a wait to retry its model request, then every 15 seconds while it stays quiet.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.maxF: The field of that entry with how many tries it makes in all. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.stat: The field of that entry's error with the HTTP status that refused the request (429: rate-limited). With none, the service couldn't be reached. Wrong, every wait shows as the service unreachable.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.subt: The kind of transcript entry Claude Code writes each time its model request fails and it tries again (rate-limited, or the service unreachable). Combwork reads the latest and shows the wait as the agent's status. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.wait: The field of that entry with how long Claude Code waits before the next try, in milliseconds. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
Claude Code's note in its transcript when its safety classifier stops a response, and the notice it adds for the model (#606). Wrong, Combwork misses such stops: no shield on the agent's pane, and Performance doesn't count them.

Claude Code's question after a safeguard stop, whether to switch models, told by its open dialog's choices in the lines it wrote last. Combwork shows the agent waiting for you, and why, while it is open; wrong, the agent shows only "Claude needs your permission".
settings.advanced.claude-code.screen.idl: A question Claude Code puts on its screen by itself after a turn, sending Combwork nothing ("Teach auto mode about your environment?"), as a line of its own in a dialog that replaces its input box or is drawn under it (the same words above the input box, in a prompt or a reply, aren't it). While it shows, Combwork shows the agent waiting for you with the question, and types nothing into it: Enter would answer it. Wrong, Combwork types its wakes into the question.
settings.advanced.claude-code.screen.inp: Claude Code's input box, between two rules, its first group what it holds after its prompt mark. Combwork reads it to tell that a line it typed is gone from the input (a screen of the CLI's took it), and then types it again. Wrong, such a line stays held, and nothing more is typed into the agent until you press Enter there.
settings.advanced.claude-code.signIn.sto: The error a StopFailure hook names when Claude Code's sign-in was refused (expired, revoked, an invalid key): Combwork shows the agent signed out and offers to carry on once it's renewed (#309). Any other error ends the turn as failed.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine: The plan limits' field for the 5-hour window.

The top-level fields Combwork knows Claude Code sends in its status line. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a status line with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
The status line's field with a subscription's limits (the 5-hour and weekly use the status bar shows). Wrong, Combwork shows no plan limits for Claude Code.
A limit's field with the percentage used.
The plan limits' field for the weekly window.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.d: The field of that result with what the subagent was asked to do, in a few words. Wrong, Combwork still counts it but has no description of it.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.i: The field of that result with the subagent's id, which its notification names when it ends. Wrong, Combwork doesn't count background subagents.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.l: The status of the Agent tool's result when it runs a subagent (or a workflow) in the background (#1584). Wrong, Combwork doesn't count those subagents, and shows the agent finished while they work.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.r: The field of a message's result with the id of a finished subagent the message started again. Wrong, Combwork doesn't count a resumed subagent while it works.
settings.advanced.claude-code.trust.prom: Claude Code's question before a folder's first session. Combwork shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.claude-code.turnScreen: Claude Code's line above its input when the last turn is done ("✻ Worked for 12s · done 16:52"). When Combwork missed a turn's end, it takes this on screen to mean the agent is idle; wrong, it leaves such an agent's status unknown, with Mark idle.
settings.advanced.claudeFooter.desc: Claude Code's footer in the {mode} mode ("{footer}"). Combwork reads an agent's permission mode from its footer (the mode found last on screen), and switches modes by pressing Shift+Tab until the footer shows the one wanted; wrong, Combwork doesn't see the agent in {mode}, and can't switch to it without a restart.
settings.advanced.claudeFooter.title: Footer: {mode}
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.account: The field of Codex's sign-in answer with the account a connection's folder is signed in as (empty when it is signed out). Wrong, Combwork can't tell, and its Codex connections show "Couldn't check".
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.dropEnv: The environment variables Combwork leaves out when it runs Codex on a connection (its sign-in, its checks and its agents), so a key or token set on this PC can't stand in for the connection's own login. Wrong, a variable Codex reads as a login could make a connection run as someone else.
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.emailFi: The field of Codex's account with the email a connection's folder is signed in as. Wrong, Combwork can't tell who a connection is signed in as, and can't warn when its login changes.
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.loginFi: The names of the files in a connection's folder that change when Codex signs in or out there, as a regular expression. Combwork watches them (it never reads them) and checks the connection again when one changes. Wrong, a sign-in or sign-out in an agent's pane is only found at the connection's next check.
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.planFie: The field of Codex's account with a connection's plan ("plus", "pro"), shown beside its email in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Wrong, no plan is shown.
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.readMet: The request Combwork sends Codex's app server to ask who a connection's folder is signed in as. Wrong, Combwork can't tell, and its Codex connections show "Couldn't check".
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.statusS: How long Combwork gives Codex's app server to say who a connection's folder is signed in as (`account/read`). Past it, the connection shows "Couldn't check", never signed out.
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.uneleva: Turned on, Combwork runs Codex on a connection (its agents, its Set Up and its checks) in Codex's non-admin Windows sandbox, passing -c windows.sandbox="unelevated" each time, unless the connection's own config.toml chooses a sandbox. Nothing is written to Codex's config, and Codex on its own folder (~/.codex) runs as you've set it up. What it gains: no Administrator (UAC) prompts, and setting up one Codex folder no longer resets the sandbox's shared password, which makes the others ask for Administrator permission again. What it loses: commands run as you rather than as separate sandbox accounts, and their network is blocked by environment settings only, not by the firewall. Unchanged: writes outside the project's folders are still refused, and the first time a connection works in a project it still grants its permissions over the project's files once. Either way, Codex's commands can still read other connections' login files. Windows only.
settings.advanced.codex.appServer.closeS: How long Codex's app server gets to end by itself once Combwork has its answer (a connection's sign-in check, its hooks' check). Past it, Combwork ends it with everything it started. Too short, Codex is cut off as it ends; too long, its processes stay a little longer.
settings.advanced.codex.exit.command.des: What Combwork types into Codex, then Enter, to end it once its lane has ended and its turn is over, so it exits by itself rather than being killed. Wrong, Codex isn't ended by it and is killed after the exit grace.
settings.advanced.codex.exit.graceSecond: How long Combwork gives Codex to exit by itself after typing its exit command at a lane's end, before killing it. It took {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} when recorded.
settings.advanced.codex.fullAccess.answe: How long Combwork's switch to Full Access waits for you to answer Codex's own warning in its terminal. Meanwhile Combwork types nothing into the agent; once it passes, Combwork says Codex didn't confirm the switch, and still notices it later if you answer Yes.
Full Access warning: wait for your answer
settings.advanced.codex.fullAccess.warni: Codex's own warning after Full Access is picked in its /permissions menu, which you answer in its terminal. While it is on screen, Combwork's switch to Full Access waits for your answer; if it doesn't match, Combwork may say Codex didn't confirm the switch while the warning is still waiting.

How long Codex has, after Combwork picks a preset in its /permissions menu before its first message, to show its own warning (Full Access). With no session file to read the switch back from, Combwork takes the preset as switched once this passes with no warning; raise it if a slow machine draws the warning later.
Full Access warning: time to appear
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.knownEvent: The hook events Combwork knows Codex sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.knownField: The top-level fields Combwork knows Codex sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a Codex update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.listMethod: The request Combwork sends Codex's app server for the hooks a session has. Wrong, an agent's Hooks dialog lists only Combwork's own and says Codex couldn't list the rest, and Combwork trusts its hooks by its own hashes.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.listSecond: How long Combwork gives Codex's app server to list a session's hooks (`hooks/list`). Past it, an agent's Hooks dialog lists only Combwork's own and says Codex couldn't list the rest.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.preToolUse: How long Codex waits for Combwork's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Combwork doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.timeoutSec: How long Codex waits for Combwork to take one of its hooks. Codex itself holds the interrupt and session-end hooks to {most, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} at most. Combwork approves its hooks for Codex itself, so a change needs no review in Codex.
settings.advanced.codex.mcp.startupTimeo: How long Codex waits for Combwork's combwork server to start, when your own Codex config has a server named combwork with a startup timeout of its own: Combwork gives Codex this one instead (otherwise Codex's own, 10 s, applies). Too short, and Codex agents start without Combwork's tools.
Combwork tools: startup timeout in Codex
settings.advanced.codex.mcp.toolTimeoutS: How long Codex lets one of Combwork's tools run (its tool_timeout_sec for the combwork server). Combwork's waits stay a minute under it.
settings.advanced.codex.mouse.rightClick: Right-click in a Codex pane is Combwork's, as in every pane: it copies the terminal's selection (Shift+drag), or pastes. Turned on, Combwork passes right-clicks to Codex instead, which tracks the mouse itself.
settings.advanced.codex.outage.connectio: A turn's error, in Codex's session file, that means it lost its connection to its API: with Resume agents after a connection drops on, Combwork waits for the connection and resumes the agent. Wrong, such agents stay stopped.
settings.advanced.codex.override.mcpIsol: Combwork's Codex sessions get the MCP servers the workspace gives them, and Combwork turns off the ones in your own Codex config and the project's (enabled=false, for those sessions only). Turned off, those load beside the workspace's too, as they would outside Combwork. Combwork's own combwork server always wins over one of yours with that name.
settings.advanced.codex.override.preAppr: Combwork gives Codex its combwork server with its tools approved (for the Assistant, only those its Control settings let it use without asking), so Codex doesn't ask before them in any mode. Turned off, Codex asks before them as its own approval policy says. What an agent or the Assistant may do with them is still decided by Combwork.
settings.advanced.codex.override.termina: Combwork gives Codex's sessions their terminal title items (Terminal title items, as tui.terminal_title), whatever your own Codex config says, and tells from the title when Codex needs you ("Action Required"). Turned off, your Codex config decides the title, and Combwork tells when Codex needs you from its hooks instead, as it does for Codex versions before 0.160. Codex's setup in Provider Setup keeps Combwork's title, which it waits on.
settings.advanced.codex.prompt.drawnSeco: How long Combwork waits for Codex to show a line Combwork typed (a message's notice, a wake) in its prompt before pressing Enter. Codex drops an Enter that it reads together with the line while it is busy, so Combwork presses Enter once the line shows; if it doesn't show in time, Combwork presses Enter anyway, and presses it again 10 seconds later if the line wasn't sent.
Typed line: wait to be drawn
settings.advanced.codex.prompt.newlineKe: With Send prompts as typed on, what Combwork presses in Codex for each line break of a prompt it types. Alt+Enter and Ctrl+J are keys Codex takes as a new line rather than sending, so the prompt arrives as written (tried with Codex 0.164.0). Automatic uses Alt+Enter with a Codex version it was tried with, and spaces with others; a key you choose is used with any version. Spaces puts the prompt on one line. If you changed Codex's own new-line keys, choose Spaces. A slash command always gets spaces.
settings.advanced.codex.promptInput.time: How long Combwork waits, as a Codex agent starts, for Codex to show the session's prompt (codex debug prompt-input, offline), from which it reads the developer_instructions it puts its guidance after. Too short on a slow machine, the agent starts with yours as they are and without Combwork's guidance, and Combwork says so.
settings.advanced.codex.queue.hint.desc: Codex's hint on the last line it draws while it is busy and queues what is typed. Combwork waits for it to go before typing into Codex (a message, its /permissions menu at setup); wrong, what Combwork types can be queued rather than run.
settings.advanced.codex.queue.hint.title: Screen: holding what was typed
settings.advanced.codex.rateLimits.field: The field of Codex's token counts with a subscription's limits. Wrong, Combwork shows no plan limits for Codex.
settings.advanced.codex.rateLimits.usedP: A limit's field with the percentage used.
settings.advanced.codex.rateLimits.windo: A limit's field with its window in minutes (300 is the 5-hour limit, 10080 the weekly one).
settings.advanced.codex.ready.placeholde: The text Codex's empty input shows. Codex only says it has started with the first prompt, so Combwork takes this text on screen to mean it is ready, and an input line showing only this to mean it is idle.
settings.advanced.codex.retry.checkAfter: How long a working Codex session has to go without a hook before Combwork looks in Codex's log for a wait to retry its model request, then every 15 seconds while it stays quiet.
Where in its own log (logs_2.sqlite in its home folder) Codex says it is waiting to retry its model request, after being rate-limited for example. Combwork reads the latest such entry of a session's turn and shows the wait as its status. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.codex.retry.pattern.de: How Codex words that log entry: a regular expression whose named groups give the try (attempt), the tries allowed (max), the wait (seconds, or millis) and the HTTP status that refused the request (status: 429 is a rate limit). Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.codex.signIn.expired.d: A turn's error, in Codex's session file, that means its sign-in was refused or has expired, when Codex doesn't mark the error itself (#309).
settings.advanced.codex.subagent.item.de: The kind of item Codex records when a subagent it spawned starts or ends (#1584). Wrong, Combwork doesn't count Codex's subagents among an agent's background tasks.
settings.advanced.codex.subagent.started: The kind of that activity when the subagent starts; any other kind ends it. Wrong, Combwork doesn't count Codex's subagents.
settings.advanced.codex.subagent.taskFie: The field of that activity with the subagent's task name. Wrong, Combwork still counts it but has no description of it.
settings.advanced.codex.subagent.threadF: The field of that activity with the subagent's thread, which tells its start and its end apart from another's. Wrong, Combwork doesn't count Codex's subagents.
settings.advanced.codex.title.items.desc: What Combwork asks Codex to put in its terminal title (tui.terminal_title): its activity, which shows the busy spinner and "Action Required", and the project's name. Without activity, Combwork can't tell from the title that Codex is working or needs you.
Each Codex agent is started with its own folder (its project, slot or review copy) trusted for that launch, so Codex doesn't ask whether to trust it. Nothing is written to Codex's files. Off, Codex asks once per project on each connection, and Set Up walks you through them.
Trust Combwork's folders on each launch
settings.advanced.codex.trust.prompt.des: Codex's question before a folder's first session (in a Git repository). Combwork shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.codex.turnScreen.worki: Codex's Working line, drawn only while a turn runs. When Combwork missed a turn's start or end, it takes this on screen to mean the agent is working; wrong, it can take a working agent for idle.
settings.advanced.codexPermissions.desc: The label Codex's /permissions menu shows for its {label} preset. Combwork types the number beside it to give an agent the {mode} mode; wrong, Combwork can't find it, and says so rather than choosing another.
settings.advanced.codexPermissions.title: /permissions menu: {label}
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.con: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the conversation's tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sum: The field of a compaction's end, in Copilot's session file, with the summary it carries on from: the Sessions tab shows it with the compaction.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sys: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the system prompt's tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.too: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the tool definitions' tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.exit.armed.des: What Copilot shows after one Ctrl+C at its prompt, meaning the next one exits. When Combwork stops Copilot, it presses Ctrl+C again once this shows. If it no longer matches, Combwork keeps pressing Ctrl+C until Copilot exits, which takes longer.
settings.advanced.copilot.exit.graceSeco: When Combwork stops Copilot (Stop, Restart, closing a project or quitting), how long it gives Copilot to exit by itself after its Ctrl+C before killing it. Copilot writes the session's token totals only as it exits by itself: one killed first loses them. It took up to {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} on a busy machine (#716); quitting Combwork or closing a workspace waits up to this long, and a second more, for a Copilot that hangs.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownEve: The hook events Combwork knows GitHub Copilot sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownFie: The top-level fields Combwork knows GitHub Copilot sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a GitHub Copilot update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.preToolU: How long Copilot waits for Combwork's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Combwork doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.timeoutS: How long Copilot waits for Combwork to take one of its hooks.
settings.advanced.copilot.mouse.rightCli: Right-click in a Copilot pane is Combwork's, as in every pane: it copies the terminal's selection (Shift+drag), or pastes. Turned on, Combwork passes right-clicks to Copilot instead, which copies its own selection (a drag) with them, as its footer says.
settings.advanced.copilot.outage.connect: What Copilot's error says when it couldn't reach its model's API after its retries: with Resume agents after a connection drops on, Combwork waits for the connection and resumes the agent. Wrong, such agents stay stopped.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.allMc: Combwork starts Copilot with --allow-all-mcp-server-instructions, so Copilot puts the combwork server's instructions (Combwork's guidance for agents) in its system prompt, and the instructions of the other servers its agents get too. Turned off, Copilot includes only the servers it allows by itself, and Combwork gives its guidance as custom instructions instead.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.mcpIs: Combwork starts Copilot with --disable-builtin-mcps, and --disable-mcp-server for each server in your own Copilot config and the project's, so its sessions get only the MCP servers the workspace gives them. Turned off, those and Copilot's built-in GitHub servers load beside them, as they would outside Combwork. The workspace's servers, Combwork's own combwork server among them, win over yours of the same name.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.noAut: Combwork starts Copilot with --no-auto-update and COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false (its sessions, and checking its sign-in and models), so it runs the version installed and a download never changes it between a session's restarts; Update in Provider Setup updates it when you choose. Turned off, Combwork sets neither and Copilot updates itself as it would outside Combwork (your own COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE still applies).
settings.advanced.copilot.override.preAp: Combwork starts Copilot with --allow-tool for Combwork's tools (for the Assistant, only those its Control settings let it use without asking), so Copilot doesn't ask before them in any mode. Turned off, Copilot asks before them as its own permission mode says. What an agent or the Assistant may do with them is still decided by Combwork.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.strip: Combwork leaves GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, which other tools set, out of Copilot's environment, so a token left there never signs Copilot agents in to another account; COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, set for Copilot, is kept. Turned off, Copilot gets them and signs in with them before its own login, as it would outside Combwork, and Provider Setup shows that sign-in.
Keep GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN from Copilot
settings.advanced.copilot.question.field: The field of the question tool's input, in Copilot's hooks, with the question's text. When it is wrong, the agent shows only Copilot's own notice while it waits for your answer.
The name Copilot's hooks give its tool that asks you a question. Combwork shows that tool's question while the agent waits for your answer; when it doesn't match, the agent shows only Copilot's own notice.
settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.d: Copilot only says it has started with the first prompt, so Combwork takes its footer on screen to mean it is ready.
Where Copilot's error hook says a recoverable error happened when it is a model call it tries again (rate-limited, or the service unreachable). Combwork shows the agent's status as waiting to retry until Copilot goes on. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
How that hook words why the call failed: a regular expression whose named group status is the HTTP status that refused it, whose group limited matches the words of a rate limit (429), or whose group network matches when the service couldn't be reached. Copilot's hook gives the service's own error, often with no status. Wrong, the wait shows without its reason.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorMe: A session error's message, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused, when its type doesn't say so.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorTy: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused or is missing (#309): Combwork shows the agent signed out.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.hookMes: The message of Copilot's ErrorOccurred hook that means a model call was refused for the sign-in: the turn ends signed out. Another error that ends the turn ends it as failed.
settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.d: Copilot's question before a folder's first session. Combwork shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.copilot.turnFailed.err: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its turn ended because a model call failed after Copilot's retries (it sends no Stop then): Combwork ends the turn as failed, with Copilot's message. Wrong, such an agent shows working until you look.
settings.advanced.copilotFooter.desc: Copilot's footer in the {mode} mode ("{footer}"){shared, select, yes {, which Ask and Accept edits share (Combwork tells them apart by the mode the session started in)} other {}}. Combwork reads an agent's mode from its footer (the mode found last on screen), and switches modes by pressing Shift+Tab until the footer shows the one wanted; wrong, Combwork doesn't see the agent in that mode, and can't switch to it without a restart.
settings.advanced.copilotFooter.title: Footer: {mode}
settings.advanced.data.tip: Project settings live in each project's .combwork folder; workspace settings in the workspace .combwork folder.
settings.advanced.data.title: Settings file
settings.advanced.error.field: {title} takes a field name: letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit).
settings.advanced.error.folder: {title} takes one folder's full path (C:\…, \\server\…, or starting with a variable such as %LOCALAPPDATA%).
settings.advanced.error.folders: {title} takes up to {most} folders, each a full path (C:\…, \\server\…, or starting with a variable such as %LOCALAPPDATA%), separated by semicolons.
settings.advanced.error.list: {title} takes 1 to 10 names (letters, digits, - and _), as a list or separated by commas.
settings.advanced.error.matchesAll: {title} would match anything (it matches empty text).
settings.advanced.error.number: {title} takes a whole number from {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.error.oneLine: {title} takes one line of at most {most} characters.
settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov: Move an account's agents to another account when it reaches the share of its limit set on it in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Turned off, no account moves its agents and moves waiting for an agent's turn to end are dropped; the rules are kept.
Move agents at a usage threshold
settings.advanced.hive.agents.perProject: How many agents a project can have (#562): {usual} unless you need more, up to {most}. Each agent runs its own copy of its CLI, so more agents take more memory, and they all share your plans' usage limits. Lowering it removes no agents: a project with more just can't add another. Templates and the Agent API keep to it too.
settings.advanced.hive.agents.tempFolder: A folder for agents' own temporary files (Claude Code's scratchpad, and what Codex, Copilot and their shells write to the temp folder), instead of Windows' Temp folder: each agent and the Assistant get a folder of their own in it, made at launch, and kept. A full path (%LOCALAPPDATA% and other variables at the start are filled in), never inside a project or a slot. Empty: the system's Temp folder, as before. Sessions started afterwards take it.
settings.advanced.hive.assistant.otherMc: The Hive Assistant looks after the workspace with Hive's own tools only: the workspace's other MCP servers aren't given to it. Turned on, it gets every server that is on in the workspace (its switch in the MCP view), from its next session, as it works across every project. Its Control setting still decides what it may do with Hive's tools; another server's tools ask as its CLI's permission mode says. Whether its CLI's own servers load too is the CLI's "Only the workspace's MCP servers" setting.
The Assistant uses the workspace's other MCP servers
settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi: While the Assistant's journal is on, Combwork gives it a short view of the workspace when it starts and after each compaction: what is under way and waiting, and the journal's recent entries. Turned off, it gets none from its next start or compaction on, a running Assistant too, and reads what it needs with its tools.
The Assistant starts with Combwork's start view
settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentF: More folders an agent, the Assistant or a script may attach files to a card from, besides its own project's folders and the temp folder: full paths, separated by semicolons (%LOCALAPPDATA% and other variables at the start are filled in). Another project's folders and Combwork's own stay refused, even inside one. Empty: none.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentM: The largest file Combwork keeps with a card, in bytes: pasted or dropped into the card, attached from an agent's pane, or given by an agent or the Assistant. A larger file is refused, saying so. Files already kept stay.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.titleNudgeC: When an agent or the Assistant gives a card a title longer than this, Combwork keeps it and tells the agent a shorter one would be better: a long title is cut in git's history, where it becomes the merge commit's subject, and on the board. The titles you write yourself are never questioned. 0 turns the suggestion off.
Show the text in the developer console: prompts, replies, commands and tools' arguments, under a banner saying it is unredacted, and start each recording with its text box ticked. Tokens, API keys and sign-in details stay masked whatever this says; agents' cw_console stays redacted, and a recording with text is never attached to Copy Diagnostics.
Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text
settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM: A returned review or check copy is used again only once nothing is running in it: no run, no process its check started, its reviewer idle. Past this many minutes, a check waiting for a copy says which copy is still in use and by what. Combwork never resets a copy something is still running in.
Copies: wait for one to be free
settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.des: A reviewer reads a card's work, and runs its commands, in a review copy: a folder at exactly the revision under review, which nothing else writes, so what it checks is what was submitted. Turned off, reviewers read the builder's folder as before. Isolated checks (cw-progress --check with --isolated) use the same copies either way.
settings.advanced.hive.disableHardwareAc: Draw Combwork without the graphics card, for a graphics driver that leaves Combwork's window blank, flickering or crashing. Terminals then draw without WebGL. Takes effect when Combwork restarts; to start once without it, run Combwork with --disable-gpu.
settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon: How long the project’s command that chooses a card’s focused tests may run, when it is submitted and at its merge. Past it, the command is ended and no tests count as chosen: the builder then names them itself.
Focused tests: longest the choice of tests runs
settings.advanced.hive.guidance.desc: With Combwork's tools, each project agent gets Combwork's guidance: how to use the tools, the board and handovers, and its project's latest handover. Claude Code and Copilot get it as the combwork server's instructions, Codex after your own developer_instructions. Turned off, agents still get Combwork's tools, without the guidance, from their next session. The Assistant always gets its own: they are its role.
settings.advanced.hive.guidance.title: Combwork's guidance for agents
settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL: When Combwork's main process nears its memory limit, it writes a snapshot of its memory to the heap folder in Combwork's profile before it closes, to find out what filled it. A snapshot can be several gigabytes, holds whatever Combwork had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens) and stays on this PC; Combwork keeps the newest two. Takes effect when Combwork restarts.
Save a memory snapshot if Combwork is about to run out of memory
settings.advanced.hive.hooks.missingSeco: How long an agent's CLI may go without a hook, from its start (a CLI that sends one then) or from a prompt it went to work on, before Combwork says its hooks aren't arriving and shows its status as unknown (#1336). A long think after a prompt's hook never counts. Raise it if a slow machine shows that notice for agents that are fine.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints: When something arrives in a working agent's inbox, Combwork tells it at the end of its next tool call, in that tool's reply, so it can read it without stopping. Turned off, a working agent isn't told until its turn ends or it is idle; nothing is lost, as it stays in the inbox. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
Tell a working agent at the end of a tool
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.d: When something arrives in an idle agent's inbox, Combwork types one short line into its terminal saying so, which wakes it. Card loops' wakes (the workflow option Wake reviewers and builders) and card watches' are such wakes. Turned off, nothing is typed for anything waiting: it stays in the inbox, the agent's pane shows how many, and its Deliver Now types the line once. A card started on an agent, or a task given to it now, is still typed. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu: When an agent is about to end its turn with items in its inbox it hasn't read, Combwork keeps it going to read them first, once a turn: Codex and Copilot by holding their stop back, Claude Code by adding a line to its stop. Turned off, the turn ends as the CLI ends it, and the items wait in the inbox for an idle wake. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items
settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.de: When Combwork's own installer is built from its source code (npm run dist, or npm run release), Combwork writes the build into the Assistant's journal as its own entry: the version, the commit, what kind of build it was and where the installer is. Only a successful build is written, and only while the journal is on with events in its scope. Turned off, builds aren't written, and a build left for Combwork while it was closed is dropped when the workspace opens.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu: How long, from a lane's end, Combwork waits for its builder to finish its turn and read that the lane is finished. Past it, Combwork ends the builder's CLI anyway: with its exit command, or killed when that can't be typed (your draft is in its prompt) or doesn't end it.
Lanes: longest a lane's end waits for its builder
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW: A lane starts its agents in new conversations. One that is busy as the lane starts (in a turn, or reading a message Combwork just gave it) is started once it is free, for up to this long. After that Combwork stops trying: the lane's row says so, and you retry it there or end the lane. Combwork never interrupts a turn for it, and never gives the lane's cards to the old conversation.
Lanes: longest Combwork waits to start a busy agent afresh
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.d: When a lane's last card merges (or the lane is abandoned), Combwork waits for its builder's turn to end, tells it the lane is finished with each card's merge commit, then ends its CLI with the CLI's own exit command, killing it only if it doesn't exit. Its slot stays its until then. Turned off, Combwork stops the builder's session as soon as it is first idle, as before.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.t: Lanes: let the builder finish when its lane ends
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo: When the Assistant may control agents (Settings → Assistant → Control) and is about to end its turn while lanes are running and no watch of its covers them, Combwork keeps it going once to say so, naming the lanes' builders, so it watches them before it finishes. At Look and advise the lanes are yours to run, and it isn't told. Turned off, its turn ends as its CLI ends it, and nothing wakes it about those lanes until it watches them again.
Lanes: remind the Assistant to watch them
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe: After how long a lane whose card waits in Review with nobody reviewing it has its wait marked in the Progress panel's Lanes. Too short marks every review; too long, a card can sit unreviewed.
Lanes: a long wait for a reviewer
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu: After how long a lane waiting for you (a request in For you, or a card at its round limit) has its wait marked in the Progress panel's Lanes. Too short marks every wait; too long, a lane can sit unnoticed.
Lanes: a long wait for you
settings.advanced.hive.lostLine.steadySe: A line Combwork typed into an agent that its CLI didn't take, gone from its input since (a screen of the CLI's took it): how long its input must stay empty, at its prompt, with nothing taken, before Combwork types it again or, with nothing to type again, tells you. Raise it if a slow machine has a line typed twice.
settings.advanced.hive.mcp.connectSecond: How long Combwork waits, once an agent is ready, for its CLI to connect Combwork's tools before it tells the agent of new work anyway. A resumed session can be ready before its tools are, and a message then is a turn spent without them (#865). Lower it if messages reach agents late when their CLI doesn't connect Combwork's tools.
How long the combwork MCP server waits for Combwork to answer one of its tools (a wait's own time comes on top). Raise it when a slow or very busy machine makes Combwork tools fail with "Combwork didn't reply within 300 s" (#371).
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.downlo: How long Install and Update wait for a catalogue server's zip, redirects included, before they stop with nothing installed. Raise it on a slow connection.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.fetchS: How long the MCP view waits for a catalogue's list, redirects included, before it shows that catalogue couldn't be read. Raise it on a slow connection.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS: How long each check of this PC for a catalogue server's requirements (its Windows edition and build, Node.js, Docker) may take before it shows as not checked.
MCP catalogues: checking this PC's requirements
settings.advanced.hive.merge.lockWaitSec: How long a merge, or another change to a repository's branches (a pull, switching branch, moving an agent's branch), waits while another Combwork on this computer is merging into the same repository. After it, nothing is changed and Combwork says which Combwork holds the repository: try again once it has finished. Combwork never takes the repository from a Combwork that is still running.
settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco: In a project without version control, Combwork reads the project's files in the background when a card starts, when it is submitted, and when a check of it starts and ends, to find what changed outside the card's files. A read that takes longer than this is stopped: the card starts or is submitted without that list, and the check doesn't count.
No version control: longest read of the project
settings.advanced.hive.notes.deliverWork: Each agent and the Assistant get the shared note Workspace notes in their instructions when they start, on every CLI and in whichever folder they work: notes about this machine that no committed file should hold. A project's agents get the parts for everyone and their own project's section. Turned off, or with the note empty, nothing is added, from each agent's next session.
settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo: How much of the shared note Workspace notes an agent's instructions get, at most, in bytes. A longer note is cut, and agents are told to read the note for the rest. Every agent reads it at every start, so a short note costs less.
Workspace notes: most an agent gets
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst: How long after the turn ends Combwork first checks the connection. Each check that finds it still down doubles the wait before the next, up to the longest wait below.
Resuming after a connection drops: first check after
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS: The longest Combwork waits between two checks of the connection.
Resuming after a connection drops: longest wait between checks
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c: The address Combwork asks to see whether Claude Code's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too. An agent on a server connection is checked at its server's address instead.
Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Claude Code
The address Combwork asks to see whether Codex's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too.
Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Codex
The address Combwork asks to see whether GitHub Copilot's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too.
Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for GitHub Copilot
settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect: A failed turn whose error this regular expression finds is never resumed, whatever a CLI's connection error pattern finds: a usage or rate limit, a sign-in, an overloaded server. Resuming wouldn't help those, and could repeat.
Resuming after a connection drops: errors that are never a dropped connection
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.des: When an agent's turn ends because its CLI couldn't reach its API (a router restarting, Wi-Fi dropping), Combwork shows it waiting for the connection, checks the CLI's API host now and then, and once it answers tells the agent to rerun what was cut off and carry on. Never for a usage limit, an expired sign-in or an overloaded server. After three resumes in an hour that end the same way, or once the wait's limit passes, Combwork stops and says what to try.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.tit: Resume agents after a connection drops
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer: How many times in an hour Combwork resumes the same agent. Once its turn ends on a connection error again after that many, Combwork stops: the PC's own network may not have recovered.
Resuming after a connection drops: resumes in an hour
settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute: How long Combwork waits for the connection to come back before it stops waiting and tells you.
Resuming after a connection drops: wait at most
settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN: When a process an agent's command started is still running ten minutes on with the shell that started it gone, Combwork says so once in a notice, and tells the agent once at its next tool call or turn's end, so it can end it. Turned off, neither is told; Activity still lists the process as left running, with End It.
Processes left running: tell me and the agent
settings.advanced.hive.progress.lanesSho: How many card-loop lanes the Progress panel shows before its lanes scroll, until you drag the section's top edge (the drag is kept per workspace). A workspace that runs many lanes at once can set its own.
settings.advanced.hive.progress.replySec: How long cw-progress waits for Combwork to answer before a command or a check starts, and for its start to be taken. A check needs the answer (its command is the project's): with none, it asks once more, then runs nothing and says Combwork is slow. Raise it when a busy Combwork makes checks fail with "Combwork is slow to answer" (HI-1892). Kept at 2 minutes at most.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.de: Combwork puts each prompt it types into an agent (a message, a wake, a card's start) on one line: runs of spaces become one, line breaks become spaces, and control characters are left out. Turned on, Claude Code and Copilot get the text as written, spacing and line breaks included. Codex, and a slash command in any CLI, still get each line break and tab as a space: Combwork types those key by key, where a line break would send the prompt early and a tab complete a word. For Codex, Typed prompts: line breaks (under Codex) can press a new-line key instead. Other control characters are left out either way: they would press keys.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft: Before Combwork types a prompt or Compact into an agent's CLI, it presses Ctrl+U, which clears what is in the CLI's input, and it presses it again to take back a prompt it stopped part-way. Turned off, Combwork never presses it: text left in the CLI's input stays in front of what Combwork types and is sent with it, a prompt stopped part-way stays in the input, and Compact can fail behind a draft. Changing Codex's mode still clears its input first, as its menu needs.
Clear the CLI's draft before Combwork types
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta: When a card is started on an agent, Combwork gives it the card wrapped in its own words: which card it is on the board, what it depends on and which docs to read first, and which skill to follow. Turned on, the agent gets only the card's title and description, and what you wrote when you started it. Combwork's other prompts (its wakes and messages) stay as they are: they are how Combwork and its agents talk.
A card's start in its own words
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute: How long the merge queue lets one merge check or install run before it ends it. A check ended this way is a failure of the environment, not of the work: the card comes back marked so, and its builder can send the same revision back into the queue. Raise it when a project’s checks really take longer; too long, and a hung check holds the queue up that long.
Merge queue: longest a merge check runs
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT: When the branch the merge queue merges into is checked out in a folder (the project folder's main, say), merging changes that folder's files too. Ask each time waits, once a card is tested and ready, for you to approve updating the folder in For you. Automatically updates it at once. Either way the queue first checks that no agent is working in the folder, that it is on that branch and that you have no changes in the files the merge changes, and pauses if not. One rare race, another program switching that folder's branch in the same instant, can leave the merged files in the other branch; Combwork then says so and lists them. A branch checked out nowhere is always merged at once.
Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch
settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs: How many tests at once the merge queue’s run of a card’s focused tests may use, passed to the project’s command that runs them. More finishes sooner but loads the computer, which agents and your own work share.
Merge queue: focused tests run at once
settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode: A failed merge check whose last 40 lines of output this regular expression finds failed for the network, not the work: the card is returned to its builder marked temporary, and the builder may submit the same revision again (at most twice in a row) instead of a new one. The default finds Node's and npm's network error codes (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT). A project's check can also say so itself by exiting with code 75. (?!) finds nothing: then only a check that couldn't start, ran out of time or was ended counts as temporary.
Merge queue: network errors that count as temporary
settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds: When a repository signs its commits, how long the merge queue waits for its merge commit, hooks included, before it takes the signer to be waiting for a passphrase. It then ends the commit, changes nothing in the target and pauses the queue with “signing waits for you”. Raise it when signing or the repository’s commit hooks really take longer; too long, and a signer waiting for you holds the queue up that long.
Merge queue: longest a signed merge commit takes
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec: How long a capture waits after its trigger before it is saved, so it holds what followed too: what the CLI did next.
Flight recorder: wait after a trigger
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.keep.des: How many captures Combwork keeps in its console-recordings folder: past it, the oldest go. Recordings you made in the developer console are never removed.
How long after a capture the same trigger waits before it captures the same agent again, so something that keeps happening saves one capture, not many.
Flight recorder: one capture per trigger and agent every
Save a capture when an agent's developer console event has a name or summary this regular expression finds (case-insensitive). The default, (?!), never finds anything: it is off.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.safeguar: Save a capture when a model's safeguards stop a response or switch the model: the agent's newest developer console events, redacted, in Combwork's console-recordings folder, with a notice. With any flight recorder trigger on, Combwork keeps each agent's newest developer console events in memory (redacted), whether a console is open or not.
Save a capture when an agent working on a turn goes silent past its limit, so Combwork can't tell what it is doing.
Flight recorder: capture an agent gone silent
Save a capture when a CLI sends a hook or a status line with a field Combwork doesn't know: often the first sign that a CLI update changed something.
Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI
Save a capture when an agent starts on a version of its CLI other than the one the last agent of that CLI started on.
Flight recorder: capture a CLI version change
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeAft: When Combwork restarts for an update (Restart to Update, or an installer closing it), the agents that were working, watching their cards or in a card loop start again in their conversations, one at a time, each told where it was. Off: Combwork offers to resume them instead, as it does after you quit.
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea: How long an agent Combwork resumes after a restart has to be ready. One that isn't is stopped and listed as not resumed, and the next one starts.
Resuming after a restart: ready within
settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista: How long an agent's coding agent may keep waiting to retry its model request (rate-limited, or its service unreachable) in one turn before Combwork tells the Assistant, once a turn. 0: never.
Retry wait: tell the Assistant after
settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal: Combwork starts each session with TERM=xterm-256color, as its terminal is, and without Windows Terminal's WT_SESSION, so the CLIs draw the same whether Combwork was opened from the Start menu or a terminal (Claude Code draws ❯ rather than >). A TERM in your own environment or the session's is kept. Turned off, sessions get the environment Combwork was opened with.
Sessions say their terminal is xterm-256color
settings.advanced.hive.showDeveloperFeat: Show Help → Developer Console (Ctrl+Alt+J): what each CLI sends Combwork, next to what Combwork made of it.
settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle: Codex and Copilot read Combwork's skills from copies Combwork puts in each agent's folder (.agents/skills/cw-…); Claude Code gets them at each launch and leaves nothing behind. Once the last of Combwork's agents in a folder stops, Combwork can remove its copies, so a CLI you run there yourself doesn't see them. Slots only removes them from slots and agents' worktrees, never the project folder. Everywhere removes them from the project folder too. Never keeps them. Only copies Combwork made, and nobody changed since, are removed: never your own skills.
Remove Combwork's skill copies when no agent works in the folder
settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge: Each card built in a slot works on a branch of its own, such as cw/AM/AM-12-fix-the-login. Once the card is Done and its target branch contains the branch's work (a squash merge too), Combwork deletes the branch and notes it on the card. A branch with work that isn't merged, or checked out somewhere, is never deleted. Turned off, the branches stay.
Delete a card's branch once it's merged
A project keeps as many slots as it has builders. A free slot beyond that, unused for a day, is removed: its archive command runs first, and it is kept if that fails. Combwork never removes one with an agent or a process in it, a lease, a merge in flight, or work that isn't committed and merged. Turned off, idle slots stay until you remove them.
Remove idle slots after a day
settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt: At the upgrade to 1.0 your agents' worktrees became slots, keeping their folders (hb2). Once one is free, with no agent or process in it, Combwork renames its folder to a slot's name (slot-c), moving its cards' work and the agents' conversations with it, so a slot named after one agent isn't lent to another. Turned off, they keep their names.
Rename adopted worktrees to slot names
settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute: How long Combwork lets a slot's setup command, a dependency install or its archive command run before it ends it. A slot whose setup was ended this way isn't lent until it is set up again; an archive command ended so keeps its slot.
Slots: longest a setup command runs
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT: In an agent's pane, Combwork's own shortcuts (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts) take their keys, apart from those the CLI uses itself. Turned on, every key goes to the CLI, except the command palette's shortcut (Show All Commands), which stays Combwork's so every command is still in reach. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V have their own setting.
All keys go to the CLI
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo: In an agent's pane, Ctrl+C copies the terminal's selection (with nothing selected it goes to the CLI, which stops what it is doing), and Ctrl+V pastes the clipboard's text, or a screenshot as an attachment. Turned on, both keys go to the CLI, as in any other terminal: copy and paste with right-click instead, unless right-click goes to the CLI too (a setting under each CLI).
Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.de: An agent's CLI can put text on the clipboard (OSC 52) just after you press a key or click in its pane, as Copilot does when you copy its own selection. Allow takes it at once; Ask each time shows you the text first, to copy or not; Block takes none. A CLI can never read the clipboard, whatever this says.
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.ti: A CLI putting text on the clipboard
settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet: How long the usage history keeps when each request happened, to the second, after a session ends. Past it, a session's use over time is kept in 1-hour steps, so the history stays small. Totals, tokens and costs stay exact; only where a card's or lane's share began or ended inside an hour is less exact, for sessions that old.
Usage history: keep full detail for
settings.advanced.hive.wait.agentsMaxSec: The longest cw_wait_for_agents waits for agents to finish before it answers. Kept a minute below Codex's timeout for Combwork tools, as card waits are.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.cardMaxSecon: The longest an agent's cw_wait_for_tasks call (without wake) waits before it answers. It has to stay under the CLIs' own tool timeouts, so Combwork keeps it a minute below Codex's timeout for Combwork tools whatever is set here.
Combwork keeps each project's workflow rules as cards move: what its Version Control options ask for before a card reaches Review, Approved or Done, and what follows when Combwork sees a card's work merged or changed outside Combwork. Turned off, every rule is off at once in every project: cards move wherever they are put, nothing is refused or asked, and Combwork only records what happens to each card's work, without moving cards or waking agents for it.
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg: When a card from an agent's own worktree was squashed into its target, the agent's branch still has its commits, so its next card in the lane would include them. On, Combwork moves the branch to the target before the next card starts, once the agent is idle, its runs have ended and its worktree is clean, and only when everything on it is in the target: anything else, it asks you under For you. Off, Combwork asks you every time: approve to let it move the branch once, or decline and do it yourself. Combwork never moves a branch with workflow rules turned off.
Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge
settings.advanced.logs.desc: Open the folder containing Combwork's log files.
settings.advanced.logs.title: Logs
settings.advanced.miss.field: {cli} {version} sent no field "{field}" here (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.list: {cli} {version} sent {missing}, which this list doesn't have (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.text: It doesn't find what {cli} {version} showed ("{shown}"). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.reset.desc: Restore every setting in Settings to its default, the advanced settings in advanced.json too. Workspaces and projects, and a workspace's own advanced values, are not affected.
settings.advanced.reset.tip: Recent workspaces and window position are kept.
settings.advanced.reset.title: Reset all settings
For power users and for developing Combwork. The console opens in a window of its own; Combwork captures a source only while it is open on it, redacted. Turning this off closes it.
settings.advanced.takes.folder: A folder's full path (a variable such as %LOCALAPPDATA% at the start is filled in).
settings.advanced.takes.folders: Folders, each a full path, separated by semicolons (a variable such as %LOCALAPPDATA% at the start is filled in).
settings.advanced.takes.number: A whole number of {unit, select, s {seconds} lanes {lanes} agents {agents} other {units}}, {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.values.desc: Details Combwork relies on that a CLI update can break (the text of its prompts, the fields it sends), and timeouts and limits for power users. Change one only when something doesn't work, or Combwork's notes on a CLI update say to.
settings.advanced.values.tip: Each shows its default beside it once changed, and Reset puts the default back. A value that isn't valid is ignored, with a warning, and the default used. They are kept in advanced.json in your Combwork profile, which you can also edit by hand (Open advanced.json): Combwork reads it again when it changes. A value for a CLI records the CLI version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed. Some take a workspace's own value too.
settings.advanced.values.title: Advanced settings
settings.advancedList.alsoSetting: Combwork's setting {key}, kept in advanced.json too.
settings.advancedList.cliOff: {cli} is turned off: these settings apply once you turn it on
settings.advancedList.cliVersion: It is {cli}'s: a change records the version it was made for.
settings.advancedList.fileError: {problem} Combwork keeps using the values it read before; fix the file to change them.
settings.advancedList.inboxAvailable: {on, select, true {Agents can read their inbox: they have Combwork's tools (Settings → Agent API → Provide Combwork tools to sessions).} other {Agents can't read an inbox now: they need Combwork's tools (Settings → Agent API → Provide Combwork tools to sessions), so nothing is left for them and these switches don't apply.}}
settings.advancedList.label: {group}: {title}
settings.advancedList.madeFor: Made for {cli} {version}; {installed} is installed now. Check it still works, then keep it for {installed}.
settings.advancedList.notValid: Not valid, so Combwork uses the default: {problem}
settings.advancedList.unknown: advanced.json also names {ids}, which this Combwork doesn't know (a typo, or a newer Combwork's): kept in the file, not used.
settings.advancedRow.tip: {takes} null (or Reset) goes back to Combwork's default.{cli, select, yes { It is {group}'s: an override records the version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed.{tried, select, yes { Combwork tries it on what the CLI was recorded sending, and says when it doesn't find that.} other {}}} other {}}
settings.advancedRow.title: {group}: {title}
settings.advancedRow.workspaceDesc: This workspace's own value; empty uses Settings → Advanced's. {desc}
settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.conf: Any program with the API token will be able to type commands into running sessions.
settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.desc: Let API clients type into running sessions (POST /v1/projects/'{'name'}'/input).
settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.tip: Powerful: an agent in one project could drive another project's session. Keep off unless you need orchestration.
settings.agentApi.devConsole.desc: Give agents and the Assistant a read-only Combwork tool for the developer console: what their CLI sends Combwork, next to what Combwork made of it.
settings.agentApi.devConsole.tip: Each agent reads only its own sessions; the Assistant reads its workspace's agents and Combwork's own events. Combwork captures only while the developer console is open on a source (reading starts nothing), and what it captures is redacted: no prompt or reply text, commands, tokens or sign-in details. Running sessions get the tool after a restart.
settings.agentApi.devConsole.title: Let agents read the developer console
settings.agentApi.enabled.desc: Run a local HTTP API that agents and scripts can use to talk to Combwork.
settings.agentApi.enabled.tip: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only and requires the bearer token below. See Help → Agent API Reference. Turned off, the port still answers the Assistant alone (it has its own token, and Settings → Assistant → Control decides what it may do).
settings.agentApi.enabled.title: Enable Agent API
settings.agentApi.port.desc: Local port for the Agent API.
settings.agentApi.port.tip: Change this if the port is used by another program.
settings.agentApi.port.title: Port
settings.agentApi.provideHiveMcp.desc: Add the built-in "combwork" MCP server to every session.
settings.agentApi.provideHiveMcp.tip: Gives agents tools for shared notes, handovers, project status and notifications.
settings.agentApi.provideHiveMcp.title: Provide Combwork tools to sessions
settings.agentApi.status.tip: Whether the Agent API is listening.
settings.agentApi.status.title: Status
settings.agentApi.token.desc: Bearer token required by the Agent API.
settings.agentApi.token.tip: Stored in %APPDATA%\Combwork\agent-api.json, for your own scripts. Agents never get it: each session gets a token of its own, in the file that CW_API_TOKEN_FILE names.
settings.agentApi.token.title: Access token
settings.agentApi.viewers.desc: Read-only tokens for apps that show Combwork, such as Apiary: they can read everything and follow its events, and change nothing.
settings.agentApi.viewers.tip: Name each one for its app. Stored in %APPDATA%\Combwork\agent-api-viewers.json. Revoking one cuts its app off at once. Apps find a running Combwork by %APPDATA%\Combwork\agent-api-discovery.json (the address, no token).
settings.agentApi.viewers.title: Viewer tokens
settings.agents.backgroundTaskMinutes.de: Minutes an agent waits on a background task it started (such as a test run) before Combwork counts it as finished anyway.
settings.agents.backgroundTaskMinutes.ti: An agent that ends its turn while a task it started is still running shows as waiting on background tasks, not finished: Claude Code carries on by itself when the task ends. Combwork can't tell a test run from something that never ends, such as a dev server, so it stops counting a task after this long (a Monitor also when it expires). Codex isn't told when its background terminals end, so they are only counted and shown. {min, number} to {max, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
Count background tasks for up to
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.desc: What Combwork does with processes an agent started that are still running when it stops, such as a preview server or a tail -f.
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.tip: Combwork follows every process an agent's session starts, however it was started. Ask: a notification lists them and offers to end them; the agent's pane header shows them until they end or you decide. End them: Combwork ends them as the agent stops. Combwork never ends a process the agent didn't start, and asks about the ones still running when you quit.
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.title: Processes left running
settings.appearance.terminalFontFamily.d: Font family for session terminals (CSS font list).
settings.appearance.terminalFontFamily.t: Monospace fonts work best. Cascadia Code ships with Windows Terminal; Nerd Fonts add extra glyphs.
settings.appearance.terminalFontSize.des: Font size for session terminals, in pixels.
settings.appearance.terminalScrollback.d: Lines kept in each terminal for scrolling back.
settings.appearance.terminalScrollback.t: Higher values use more memory per running session.
settings.appearance.theme.tip: System follows your Windows light/dark setting.
settings.appearance.theme.title: Theme
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.desc: Font size for menus, lists and panels, in pixels.
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.tip: View → Zoom In and Zoom Out scale everything, including the terminal.
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.title: Interface font size
settings.assistant.changeSettings.desc: Let the Assistant change Combwork's settings when you ask it to, in every workspace. Whatever this says, it can read and explain them.
settings.assistant.changeSettings.tip: It suggests a setting first and changes one only when you agree. Each change is listed in its panel with the old and new value and an Undo button. It can never change its own Control, permission modes, the Agent API or what Combwork runs (CLI paths, extra arguments, setup commands): it tells you where to change those. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.changeSettings.title: Change settings
Context size, in tokens, at which the Assistant's Compact button and the context count in its footer turn orange. Never: they never do.

The Assistant usually runs a bigger context than your agents, so it has its own threshold (your agents' is Settings → Sessions → Suggest compacting above). Compacting summarises the conversation so every later message is cheaper; the full history stays in the transcript.
settings.assistant.connection.desc: Which connection the Assistant of the open workspace runs on. The workspace's default unless you choose one.
settings.assistant.connection.noWorkspac: Open a workspace to choose its Assistant's connection.
settings.assistant.connection.title: Connection (this workspace)
settings.assistant.control.desc: What the Assistant may do beyond looking and advising, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.control.tip: It never removes agents, discards worktrees or deletes projects, and never types into an agent that is working, asking you something or that you just typed in (see Pause after you type). What it does is listed in its panel, where you can undo its changes. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.control.tip.agents: Control agents: it can also add agents, change their settings, start and stop them, and give idle ones tasks, when you ask it to. Stopping a busy agent asks you first.
settings.assistant.control.tip.inbox: How the Assistant hears of its inbox follows Settings → Advanced's three inbox switches (Tell a working agent at the end of a tool, Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items, Wake an idle agent), Settings' own values: a project's don't apply to it.
settings.assistant.control.tip.look: Look and advise: it reads and suggests, and you act.
settings.assistant.control.tip.projects: Control agents and create projects: also new projects.
settings.assistant.control.title: Control
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.desc: Once you press Enter in the terminal (you sent what you typed), the Assistant may type there at once.
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip: Turn this off if you often type a line and then keep writing (e.g. answering a question, then adding more).
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.title: Enter ends the pause
settings.assistant.journal.desc: The Assistant keeps a journal in this workspace: decisions, plans, events and what it learned, recalled a few lines at a time instead of reading a long handover. Combwork adds facts: lanes, merges, unexpected closes.
