settings.assistant.journal.tip: For this workspace. Turning it off keeps the entries; Delete Journal… removes them. The Assistant's journal tools follow a change at its next start; it is told at once.
settings.assistant.journal.title: Journal
settings.assistant.mcp.descAdded: The workspace's MCP servers added for the Assistant are chosen in its own view (the Assistant on the activity bar), as a project's are in its MCP tab.
settings.assistant.mcp.title: MCP servers (this workspace)
settings.assistant.mode.desc: How the Assistant works in a new conversation (Coordinator, Planner, QA triager, Release manager, or your own), unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.mode.tip: Modes are Markdown files in each workspace (.combwork/modes): edit them, or add your own, in the Assistant view (the crown on the left). The panel switches mode at once, keeping the conversation.
settings.assistant.mode.title: Default mode
settings.assistant.panelSide.desc: Which side of the window the Assistant's panel is on, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.panelSide.tip: On the left it sits between the project list and your work, which keeps it clear of Windows notifications and other windows at the bottom right. View → Move Assistant Panel… and the panel's ⋯ menu switch it too.
settings.assistant.panelSide.title: Panel side
settings.assistant.provider.desc: The coding agent the Assistant runs, unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.provider.tip: The Assistant is independent of your project agents: a Codex Assistant can look after Claude Code agents, and the other way round.
settings.assistant.provider.title: Provider
settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc: The Assistant's watch on an agent or its card hears the first line of what you send that agent from its pane.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip: So it knows what you told the agent (an answer, a decision) without asking you again, and can record a decision on the card. Only the first line, only to the Assistant of the same workspace, and only when it is watching that agent or its card.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.title: Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent
settings.assistant.typingPause.desc: Seconds after you type in an agent's terminal before the Assistant may type there (give it a task or hand its work over).
settings.assistant.typingPause.tip: The Assistant types a task by clearing the agent's input line (Ctrl+U) and entering it, which would wipe or mix with something you were writing. During the pause it asks you instead.
settings.assistant.typingPause.title: Pause after you type
settings.assistant.withProvider.desc: The model, effort, permission mode{context, select, yes {, context} other {}} and extra arguments when the Assistant runs {provider}. Default follows {provider}'s own settings, except the mode: {mode}, where {provider} approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
settings.assistant.withProvider.tip: By default it uses the same model and effort as your agents. A lighter model or low effort saves tokens but makes it careless (for example, saying it will check on an agent later and never doing so). Its default mode is the one your agents default to, so it rarely asks. Hive's own tools never ask: what they may do is set by Control above.
settings.assistant.withProvider.title: With {provider}
settings.assistantProvider.effort.desc: Its reasoning effort with {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider} → Default effort.
settings.assistantProvider.effort.title: Effort
settings.assistantProvider.extraArgs.des: Additional {cli} command-line arguments when the Assistant runs {provider}.
settings.assistantProvider.model.desc: The model when the Assistant runs {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider} → Default model.
settings.assistantProvider.model.title: Model
settings.assistantProvider.permissionMod: Its permission mode with {provider}. Empty is {mode}, where {provider} approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
settings.assistantProvider.use200kContex: A 200K-token context window for it with {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider}.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.desc: Days a card stays in Done before Combwork archives it.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.tip: Counted from when the card last went into Done (or was brought back from the archive), not from its last change. An archived card is kept: the board's Archived list shows it, and you can bring it back. Combwork checks when a workspace opens and every hour.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.title: Archive Done cards after
settings.board.colors.desc: Pick the colour of each column.
settings.board.colors.tip: The tint on cards is a light mix of the colour with the theme, so it works in light and dark themes. Reset puts back the default.
settings.board.colors.title: Column colours
settings.board.columnColors.desc: Give each column's heading its colour and tint its cards with it.
settings.board.columnColors.tip: A card takes the colour of the column it is in. Blocked, stalled and finished cards keep their red, amber and green edge, and their text, over the tint.
settings.board.columnColors.title: Colour columns
settings.closeCommand.hint: Combwork waits for it, showing it running. A command that shouldn't hold Combwork up can start its job and return, e.g. start "" "backup.cmd".
settings.closeCommand.noWorkspace: Open a workspace to set its close command.
settings.closeCommand.onUpdate: Also when Combwork restarts to install an update
settings.commands.cantFill: {placeholders} can't be filled here: it won't run
settings.commands.name: Name
settings.commands.needed: The commands after this need it
settings.commands.noWorkspace: Open a workspace to set its commands.
settings.commands.placeholders: cmd.exe runs it. '{workspace}' becomes the workspace's folder, '{name}' its name, '{reason}' why it runs (open, window, switch, quit, update or manual), and '{project:api}' the folder of the project api. Quote them where a path may hold spaces.
settings.commands.pointAdd: Add a command to run here…
settings.connection.argsHint: Added to {cli} when an agent on it starts.
settings.connection.effortUnusable: {model} doesn't take {effort} effort any more: agents on it start without it. Edit the connection to choose a level it takes.
settings.connection.name: Name
settings.connection.tagHint: Optional, any text. When a usage move sends this account's agents to another account, each goes to the connection there with the same tag, else the same name, else its first.
settings.connection.usedBy: In use: {users}. Running ones are offered Restart once you save (Switch Now for a new permission mode).
settings.connections.add.name: Name
settings.connections.add.title: Add a {cli} account
settings.connections.masking.full: Combwork is near the most API keys it can keep masking for. Past it, a new key is refused.
settings.connections.masking.gap: Since {date}, Combwork hides every long word in its logs, recordings and exports, for good: keys saved before its masking data was reset can't be recognised any more.
settings.connections.masking.resetMessag: Combwork can no longer recognise keys saved before. From now on it hides every long word (8 characters or more with no spaces) in its logs, recordings and exports, for good, so none of them can show an old key. This can't be undone.
settings.connections.masking.unavailable: Combwork can't read the data it uses to hide your API keys in logs and exports. Until it is reset, every long word is hidden in its logs, and exports, Copy Diagnostics and recordings are refused.
settings.connections.server.cloudTip: Runs in the cloud, not on this PC: its sessions aren't free (local).
settings.connections.server.contextAdvic: {name} recommends a context length of {size, number} tokens or more for {cli}, especially in larger repositories. Set it in {name}'s own settings: Combwork doesn't change them.
settings.connections.server.keyCleared: {name}'s server changed, so its key was removed. Add the key for the new server.
settings.connections.server.keyFailedAdd: {name} was added without its key. Use Add Key on it to try again.
settings.connections.server.keyHint: Stored encrypted for your Windows account, never shown again. The agent's commands can read it from their environment.
settings.connections.server.keyLocal: Not needed for a server on this PC.
settings.connections.server.modelsHint: Each Claude name (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) runs the model ticked for it. A model can stand in for several.
settings.connections.server.moveWarn: This is another server: its key will be removed, and you add the key for this one after.
settings.connections.server.needUrl: Give the base URL in full, starting with https:// (or http:// for this PC).
settings.connections.server.needsKey: Its server needs a key: agents on it are refused until one is added.
settings.connections.server.readAfter: Read the models from the server once it is added
settings.connections.server.readDone: {n, plural, one {# model read from {name}.} other {# models read from {name}.}}
settings.connections.server.readDropped: No longer listed, so taken out: {models}
settings.connections.server.removeKeyMes: It's deleted from this PC. Agents running on it keep it until they restart; new ones are refused until a key is added.
settings.connections.server.setUpHint: The first time {cli} runs on it, it asks a few setup questions (its look, its notes). Answer them here once, or in the first agent's pane.
settings.connections.server.why.failed: The server answered with an error ({status}). Try again later.
settings.connections.server.why.forbidde: The server refused access (403): the key may not be allowed to list models. Type the models in instead.
settings.connections.server.why.redirect: The server sent Combwork elsewhere ({status}), which Combwork doesn't follow with a key. Check the base URL.
settings.connections.server.why.refused: The server refused the key (401). Replace the key, then read again.
settings.connections.server.why.shape: The server's answer isn't a model list Combwork can read. Type the models in instead.
settings.connections.server.why.stale: The account changed while its models were read. Read them again.
settings.connections.server.why.tooBig: The model list is too large to read. Type the models in instead.
settings.connections.server.why.unreacha: Couldn't reach the server: check its base URL and that it is running.
settings.fallback.levelsPerModel: {source}: each model offers its own levels; this list names them and is used for models it doesn't describe.
settings.fallback.levelsUsed: Used now: {provider} hasn't reported per-model levels.
settings.fallback.name: Name
settings.fallback.showLevels: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}})
settings.fallback.showModels: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# model} other {# models}})
settings.general.closeToTray.desc: Closing the window keeps Combwork running in the system tray so sessions continue.
settings.general.closeToTray.tip: When off, closing the window quits Combwork (asking first if sessions are running). Use File → Exit or the tray menu to quit.
settings.general.closeToTray.title: Close to tray
settings.general.commands.desc: Your own commands for Combwork as a whole: run one by hand (here, or Run Command in the command palette), or pick them for When Combwork quits, run, or for any workspace's open and close.
settings.general.commands.tip: Saved in Combwork's own settings, never in a workspace, so a repository you clone brings none that run by themselves. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.general.commands.title: Commands
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc: When to ask before quitting stops running sessions.
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip: Quitting stops every running session. Their conversations are kept and can be resumed, so by default Combwork only asks when an agent is in the middle of something (working, or waiting for your answer).
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.title: Confirm before quitting
settings.general.dateFormat.desc: How dates show in Combwork: sessions named by when they started, the session lists and their tooltips, exports.
settings.general.dateFormat.tip: System uses your Windows language's short date. Names you give sessions stay as you typed them: only the automatic ones (when a session started) follow this. How long ago something happened ("2 hours ago") stays, with the date on hover.
settings.general.dateFormat.title: Date format
settings.general.keepAwake.desc: Stop Windows from sleeping while an agent is working or waiting on background tasks, so it doesn't stop mid-task.
settings.general.keepAwake.tip: Combwork lets the PC sleep again as soon as no agent is working. The screen can still turn off and lock. On a laptop, "When plugged in" lets it sleep on battery.
settings.general.keepAwake.title: Keep the PC awake while agents work
settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc: Start Combwork automatically when you sign in to Windows.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip: Combwork starts hidden in the tray when launched at login.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.title: Launch at login
settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc: Minimising hides Combwork to the system tray instead of the taskbar.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip: Click the tray icon to bring Combwork back.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.title: Minimise to tray
settings.general.onQuit.desc: The commands Combwork runs, in order, as it quits, once every window's workspace has closed. Combwork waits for them, showing them running.
settings.general.onQuit.tip: Pick them from Commands above. '{reason}' becomes quit, or update when Combwork restarts to install an update (only with that box ticked). Don't wait, in the dialog Combwork shows, lets Combwork go on while the rest run by themselves. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.general.onQuit.title: When Combwork quits, run
settings.general.progressCommands.desc: Agents run tests, builds and other commands that take more than about 30 seconds through cw-progress without being asked, so they show in the panel. Off: only when you ask.
settings.general.progressCommands.disabl: Turn on the Progress panel to use this.
settings.general.progressCommands.tip: cw-progress runs the command unchanged (same output and exit code). Combwork's session guidance tells agents to use it, so a change applies to agents started or restarted afterwards. With the Progress panel off, agents aren't told to use it either.
settings.general.progressCommands.title: Agents show long commands in the Progress panel
settings.general.progressPanel.desc: Show long runs agents report, such as tests and builds: how far along each is and the time left, in a panel on the right and on the taskbar button.
settings.general.progressPanel.tip: Folded, the panel is a strip with a small bar per run; click it, or use Toggle Progress Panel in the command palette. Off hides the panel, the strip and the taskbar progress; agents can still report, and Combwork ignores it.
settings.general.progressPanel.title: Progress panel
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des: Open the workspace you used last when Combwork starts.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip: Sessions are never resumed automatically — only the workspace is reopened.
settings.general.showTips.desc: One tip a day about something Combwork can do, and a tip at the moments one helps.
settings.general.showTips.tip: Tips show in a small card in the bottom corner and never get in the way. Help → Tips… lists them all, whether this is on or off.
settings.general.showTips.title: Show a tip when Combwork starts
settings.general.startMinimized.desc: Start Combwork hidden in the system tray.
settings.general.startMinimized.title: Start in tray
settings.general.timeFormat.desc: How times show with the dates.
settings.general.timeFormat.tip: Applies wherever Combwork shows a time, such as a session that started today or the time a screenshot was pasted.
settings.general.timeFormat.title: Time format
settings.general.userName.desc: How Combwork names you to the Assistant when it tells it you replied to an agent ("Darren replied to B1 on #399").
settings.general.userName.tip: It goes into the Assistant's conversation, so use whatever form you like it to see. Empty uses "User".
settings.general.userName.title: Your name
settings.journal.deleteMessage: All {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} of this workspace go to the Recycle Bin. The Assistant starts again with an empty journal.
settings.journal.local: Kept on this computer only, in .combwork/assistant/journal.db, and never sent anywhere.
settings.journal.mb: MB (past it, the oldest everyday entries go first)
settings.journal.noWorkspace: Open a workspace to set its Assistant's journal.
settings.journal.offKeeps: Off, nothing is written and the Assistant's journal tools go at its next start; the entries are kept.
settings.journal.size: Now {size}, {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
settings.keybindings.editor.desc: Click the pencil (or double-click a shortcut), then press the new keys. Wait a moment after the first combination, or press a second one for a chord such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S.
settings.keybindings.editor.tip: Shortcuts need Ctrl or Alt (or are F-keys). Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Shift+Tab stay with editing and the agents' terminals. Some keys go to the agent while its terminal has focus (for Claude Code: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+G).
settings.keybindings.editor.title: Shortcuts
settings.keys.chordNext: then another key for a chord…
settings.keys.inUseDetail: When two commands share a shortcut, the first one listed that is available runs. Change the other one to avoid surprises.
settings.keys.inUseMessage: {keys} is used by {commands}. Use it here too?
settings.keys.projectNote: Changes here apply while {project} is selected, over the global shortcuts. Other commands are set in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts.
settings.keys.resetAllGlobal: {n, plural, one {Return # changed shortcut to the defaults.} other {Return # changed shortcuts to the defaults.}}
settings.keys.resetAllProject: {n, plural, one {Remove {project}'s shortcut change; it uses the global shortcuts again.} other {Remove {project}'s # shortcut changes; it uses the global shortcuts again.}}
settings.keys.terminalKey: While an agent's terminal has focus this key goes to the agent, so the shortcut only works elsewhere.
settings.mcpCatalogs.ours: Combwork's own catalogue, checked by Combwork.
settings.mcpCatalogs.remove: Remove this catalogue (its servers installed stay)
settings.mcpCatalogs.sources.desc: Each catalogue is a catalog.json at an https:// or file:// address. Turned off, its servers aren't listed (those installed stay). Combwork reads them only when the Catalogue opens or you refresh it, and checks every download against its catalogue.
settings.mcpCatalogs.sources.title: Catalogues
settings.mcpCatalogs.theirs: Its servers aren't checked by Combwork.
settings.metrics.resetDetail: The history starts again from now.
settings.metrics.resetFailed: Could not reset the performance metrics
settings.metrics.resetMessage: Clear this workspace's recorded performance metrics?
settings.notifications.bannerPosition.de: Where notifications and tips pop up in the window.
settings.notifications.bannerPosition.ti: Several stack, the newest nearest the edge. Bottom right stays left of the Assistant's panel.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.desc: Which agents, lanes and cards the window you are using pops up a notification about.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.tip: One left out is kept under the bell without popping up. With Combwork in the background, Windows notifications come whatever this says. Clicking one about another window's project brings that window up.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.title: Show pop-ups about agents for
settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.des: How long a pop-up stays, unless it waits for you.
settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.tip: One with buttons, or an error, stays at least 15 seconds. It stays while the pointer or the keyboard is on it, and while the window is in the background.
settings.notifications.chimeEnabled.desc: Play a sound when an agent finishes or needs your input.
settings.notifications.chimeEnabled.tip: Projects can override this in their settings.
settings.notifications.chimeSound.tip: Sounds are synthesised by Combwork — no audio files needed.
settings.notifications.chimeSound.title: Chime sound
settings.notifications.chimeVolume.title: Chime volume
settings.notifications.desktopNotificati: Tell you when an agent finishes or needs input, about lanes and cards, and about plan usage: a pop-up in the window you are using, else a Windows notification.

Clicking one shows what it is about. Every one shown is kept under the bell. Off, nothing is shown either way; Combwork's own messages still pop up, and the chime and the taskbar have settings of their own.
settings.notifications.flashOnWaiting.de: When an agent starts waiting for your answer while Combwork is in the background.
settings.notifications.flashOnWaiting.ti: It stops when you switch to the window. Finishing agents never flash it.
Flash the taskbar button when an agent needs input
Notify when a session completes its task.
Triggered when the agent's turn ends (its Stop hook), or for an agent waiting on background tasks it started, when they have ended.
settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.d: Notify when a session is waiting for permission or input.
settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.t: Triggered by the agent's permission prompts and questions.
settings.notifications.suggestFreshStart: A notice when a project's last lane ends, or a card is done with no lane running, and none of its agents is busy: a good moment for Start Fresh (Idle Agents).
Once each time the work finishes. Fresh conversations cost less than long ones; the old ones stay in the Sessions tab. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.desc: A badge on Combwork's taskbar button, and the window title, show how many agents need you.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.tip: The same count as the status bar: agents waiting for your input, and those that finished while you were not looking. Each window shows its own workspace.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.titl: Show a count on the taskbar button
settings.notifications.waitingBannerStay: Until you click or dismiss it, or answer the agent. Off, they close like the others.
Answering the agent anywhere (its terminal, another window) closes its pop-up, and its entry under the bell says Answered.
Pop-ups for an agent waiting for you stay until handled
settings.notifications.whileFocused.desc: What to show while you are using a Hive window. With Hive in the background, a Windows notification.
settings.notifications.whileFocused.tip: Show in Hive: a banner in the window you are using, where Windows notifications would cover the Assistant. The chime still plays either way.
settings.prices.checked: Combwork's starting prices, checked {checked}: edit them if they are out of date.
settings.prices.newPlaceholder: Model ID, e.g. a new model
settings.prices.noReports: {provider} doesn't report costs, so Combwork estimates them from these prices. Check them against <link>{company}'s pricing</link>.
settings.prices.unlistedTip: {provider} doesn't list this model now; its price stays for older sessions.
settings.project.agents.desc: The Assistant adds agents up to the project's Maximum agents (Version Control → Workflow), and you can add more yourself, up to {max, number}, each working in the project folder or a slot. Agents without their own settings use this project's.
settings.project.agents.title: Agents
settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.d: Files kept with this project's cards go to the Recycle Bin this long after a card is archived. Open and Done cards keep theirs.
settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.t: Combwork looks when the workspace opens and once a day. Bringing a card back from the archive in time keeps its files. Afterwards the card says when they were removed, and its links to them show as removed. Cards archived because their project was hidden or removed keep theirs.
settings.project.chime.desc: Play a sound when an agent in this project finishes or needs input.
settings.project.chime.title: Completion chime
settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.de: Context size (tokens) at which Compact is highlighted for this project. Empty inherits Settings → Sessions → Suggest compacting above.
settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.ti: Only changes when the Compact button turns orange; compacting is always available once the agent has finished.
settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.desc: Combwork tells a working agent of what arrives in its inbox at the end of its next tool call. Off: it isn't told until its turn ends or it is idle; nothing is lost.
settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.tip: Inherit follows Settings → Advanced → Tell a working agent at the end of a tool.
settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.title: Tell a working agent at the end of a tool
settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.desc: Combwork types a short line into an idle agent's terminal when something arrives in its inbox, card loops' wakes included. Off: nothing is typed for what waits; the agent's pane shows how many, and Deliver Now types the line once.
settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.tip: A card started on an agent, or a task given to it now, is still typed. Inherit follows Settings → Advanced → Wake an idle agent.
settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.title: Wake an idle agent
settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.d: Combwork keeps an agent ending its turn with unread items going to read them, once a turn. Off: the turn ends, and they wait in the inbox for an idle wake.
settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.t: Codex and Copilot have their stop held back, Claude Code a line added to it. Inherit follows Settings → Advanced → Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items.
Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items
settings.project.key.desc: The 2 to 4 letters this project’s cards are named by, as in {example}. If you change it, the old key still finds them.
settings.project.key.title: Project key
settings.project.keybindings.desc: Change one to give this project its own; Reset returns it to the global shortcut. Stored in the project’s .combwork folder, which is not committed.
settings.project.keybindings.title: Shortcuts
settings.project.metadata.desc: Stored in the project's .combwork/project.json (excluded from git). Changes apply to new sessions; restart a running session to apply them.
settings.project.metadata.title: Settings file
settings.project.reset.desc: Everything on this page goes back to Inherit. Agents, and skill and MCP opt-outs, are kept.
settings.project.reset.title: Reset project settings
settings.project.storage.desc: Measured in the background; Refresh measures again. The coding agents’ own transcripts (in ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot) aren’t counted, and Clean Up… and Purge… never touch them.
settings.project.storage.title: What Combwork keeps
settings.project.suggestFreshStart.desc: A notice when this project's work has finished, with Start Fresh (Idle Agents).
settings.project.suggestFreshStart.title: Suggest a fresh start
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.desc: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript is flagged for this project. Empty inherits Settings → Sessions → Warn when a transcript is over.
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.tip: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Combwork; handing the work over to a new conversation makes it short again.
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.title: Warn when a transcript is over
settings.project.workflow.desc: Pick a preset, or set each option. Each shows where its value comes from.
settings.project.workflow.platform.desc: None or Git, from the next card: Git only where a Git repository is found and no other version control is. Each keeps its own workflow options.
settings.project.workflow.platform.title: Version control
settings.project.worktreeSetup.desc: Runs in a new worktree before its agent's first session, e.g. npm install. Its output shows in the agent's pane.
settings.project.worktreeSetup.tip: Runs with cmd.exe in the worktree folder. If it fails, the pane offers to retry or to start the agent without it.
settings.project.worktreeSetup.title: Setup command
settings.projectSection.advanced.desc: Where the settings are stored, and resetting them.
settings.projectSection.advanced.label: Advanced
settings.projectSection.agents.desc: The project’s agents and the settings of each CLI they run.
settings.projectSection.agents.label: Agents
settings.projectSection.general.desc: The project’s key, which names its cards, and the provider its new agents use.
settings.projectSection.general.label: General
settings.projectSection.keys.desc: Shortcuts for project and session commands while this project is selected, over the global ones.
settings.projectSection.keys.label: Keyboard Shortcuts
settings.projectSection.sessions.desc: Compacting and notifications for this project.
settings.projectSection.sessions.label: Sessions
settings.projectSection.storage.desc: What Combwork keeps for this project: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and the agents’ worktrees. Clean Up… moves old backups and attachments to the Recycle Bin; Purge… removes everything Combwork keeps for its sessions.
settings.projectSection.storage.label: Storage
settings.provider.allowBackgroundSession: Let {provider}'s agent view move a session into its own background service. Applies to sessions started afterwards.

Off by default. In {provider}, pressing ← on an empty prompt (easy to do while moving through text) opens its agent view and moves the session into the background. Combwork can then no longer see it or stop it: Stop only closes the terminal, the session keeps running, and resuming it fails until it is stopped with "{cli} stop".
settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.d: Compare the installed version with the latest release when Combwork starts.
settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.t: Combwork never updates {provider} without asking. Standalone installs may also update themselves.
settings.provider.costSource.desc: Where a session's API-equivalent cost comes from: {provider}'s own report, or your prices in the table below.
settings.provider.costSource.tip: {provider}'s reported cost follows its own price table and updates with the CLI; Combwork never recomputes it, even when that table lags a price change. Choose your prices for your own rates (a discount, another tier). Either way the table is used for sessions with no reported cost.
settings.provider.costSource.title: Session costs
settings.provider.effortFallback.desc: The effort levels offered when {provider} doesn't report a model's own. With the CLI's answer, each model offers just the levels it takes.
settings.provider.effortFallback.tip: The value is what Combwork passes to {provider}; the name is what the pickers and footer show.
settings.provider.effortFallback.title: Effort levels (fallback)
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.co: Recommended only for disposable environments. Each project still has to choose it, and doing so asks for confirmation.
Connections will be able to run sessions where {provider} executes every command, file edit and network request without asking.
{n, plural, one {Enable the {names} option?} other {Enable the {names} options?}}
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.de: Allow connections to choose {choices}, where the agent runs every action without asking.
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.ti: {n, plural, one {Only a connection chooses {names}. When turned off, a connection that chose it launches in the CLI's own default mode and says so.} other {Only a connection chooses {names}. When turned off, a connection that chose one of them launches in the CLI's own default mode and says so.}}
{n, plural, one {Enable the {names} option} other {Enable the {names} options}}
settings.provider.enabled.tip: When off, {provider} agents stay listed but can't start, and Combwork doesn't check for its CLI.
settings.provider.enabled.title: Use {provider}
settings.provider.executablePath.desc: Full path to the {provider} CLI ({cli}.exe). Leave empty to detect it automatically.
settings.provider.executablePath.tip: Detection checks PATH and the usual install folders. Copies bundled with editor extensions (VS Code, Cursor…) are never used — Combwork requires the standalone CLI.
settings.provider.executablePath.title: CLI path
settings.provider.modelFallback.desc: Combwork asks {provider} which models it has and what each can do. This list is only used when it can't be asked (not installed, too old, or an unexpected answer).
settings.provider.modelFallback.tip: Add, remove and rename models; a custom model ID can still be typed in any model picker. Reset to defaults goes back to Combwork's list, which then follows Combwork's updates.
settings.provider.modelFallback.title: Models (fallback)
settings.provider.prices.descEstimated: Used to estimate what {provider} sessions would cost at API prices (shown with ≈ on the Overview). USD per million tokens.
settings.provider.prices.descReported: {provider} reports each session's cost itself; these prices are used for sessions without one, or for all of them with Session costs set to your prices. USD per million tokens.
settings.provider.prices.tip: Combwork's starting prices are the published ones, checked {checked}: edit any that are out of date, add models and remove them. The table lists the models {provider} has, so a new one shows with "No price" until you enter one. Combwork never fetches prices. On a subscription you are not charged these — they show how heavy the work was.
settings.provider.prices.title: API prices
settings.provider.status.tip: Where Combwork found {provider}, whether it is signed in and whether an update is available.
settings.provider.status.title: Installation
settings.providerOff.detail: Stop them now, or let them run until they are stopped. Either way no new ones start while it is off.
settings.providerOff.listFailed: Could not list the running agents
settings.providerOff.message: {n, plural, one {An agent is running {provider}: {agents}.} other {# agents are running {provider}: {agents}.}}
settings.providerOff.title: Turn off {provider}?
settings.providers.list.desc: Turn on the coding agents you want to use. Agents of a provider that is off stay listed but can't start.
settings.providers.list.tip: Each agent runs the CLI of the connection it chose (Settings → Accounts & Connections). A provider needs its CLI installed.
settings.providers.list.title: Providers
settings.resetAll.message: Every setting in Settings returns to its default, the advanced settings in advanced.json too. A workspace's own advanced values are kept.
settings.resetAll.title: Reset all settings?
settings.section.accounts.desc: An account is a sign-in Combwork keeps (signed in through the CLI's own sign-in) or a server such as DeepSeek or Ollama, reached by its base URL and key. A connection is a setup on an account: its model, effort, context, permission mode and extra arguments. Agents and the Assistant each choose a connection, and every account shares your conversations. Drag accounts into your order: a new agent gets the first connection of the first account that's on here.
settings.section.accounts.label: Accounts & Connections
settings.section.advanced.desc: Developer features, the details Combwork relies on that a CLI update can break (advanced.json), logs, data and resetting Combwork.
settings.section.advanced.label: Advanced
settings.section.agentApi.desc: Local API and built-in MCP server that let agents interact with Combwork.
settings.section.agentApi.label: Agent API
settings.section.agents.desc: Defaults for every project’s agents: how long background tasks count, and processes agents leave running.
settings.section.agents.label: Agents
settings.section.appearance.label: Appearance
settings.section.assistant.desc: The Assistant's defaults: the side panel's overseer of each workspace (Ctrl+Alt+I). Each workspace can change them in the panel's Assistant Settings.
settings.section.assistant.label: Assistant
settings.section.board.desc: The task board's colours and housekeeping, the same in every workspace.
settings.section.board.label: Board
settings.section.general.label: General
settings.section.keybindings.desc: Change, remove or add shortcuts for any command. Projects can set their own for project and session commands (Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).
settings.section.keybindings.label: Keyboard Shortcuts
settings.section.mcpCatalogs.desc: Where the MCP view's Catalogue finds servers to install. Combwork's own comes first; add a company's or a community's list by its address.
settings.section.mcpCatalogs.label: MCP Catalogues
settings.section.notifications.desc: Chimes and desktop notifications when agents finish or need you.
settings.section.notifications.label: Notifications
settings.section.provider.desc: The {provider} CLI (the standalone one — copies bundled with editor extensions are not used): where it is, its updates, its fallback lists and prices. Models, effort and modes are on connections.
settings.section.providers.desc: The coding agents Combwork can run. Turn on the ones you use; each has its own page below with its CLI. Models, effort and modes are on connections (Accounts & Connections).
settings.section.providers.label: Providers
settings.section.sessions.desc: Transcript backups, cache estimates and session behaviour.
settings.section.sessions.label: Sessions
settings.section.updates.desc: Keeping Combwork itself up to date. New versions come from Combwork's GitHub releases and are verified before they install.
settings.section.updates.label: Updates
settings.section.workflow.desc: The workflow options projects start from: Combwork defaults, for every workspace, and the open workspace’s over them. A project’s own options, in its Version Control tab, win over both.
settings.section.workflow.label: Version Control
settings.section.workspace.desc: The open workspace's own: its projects that Combwork leaves out (hidden, or removed from Combwork with their handovers and cards packed into the folder), how much Combwork keeps for each project, and antivirus scanning. Its workflow defaults are in Version Control.
settings.section.workspace.label: Workspace
settings.sessions.backupRetention.desc: How long Combwork keeps its backups of sessions the CLI still has. After that many days without activity they go to the Recycle Bin. A session whose only copy is Combwork's backup is never touched.
settings.sessions.backupRetention.tip: Only Combwork's own copies go: the CLI's transcript stays, so the session can still be opened and resumed, and what it used stays in the usage history. To remove sessions whose only copy is Combwork's, delete them yourself or use Clean Up in Storage.
settings.sessions.backupRetention.title: Keep transcript backups
settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.desc: Copy each session's transcript into the project's .combwork/sessions folder.
settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.tip: Agents delete old transcripts after a while (Claude Code: 30 days by default). Backups let you resume and review sessions later. Archived sessions are always preserved.
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.desc: Used to estimate whether resuming a session needs to re-cache its context.
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.tip: Auto detects the cache type from the transcript (5 minutes or 1 hour).
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.d: Context size, in tokens, at which the context in an agent's pane footer turns orange. Never: it never does.
settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.t: Compacting summarises the conversation so every later message is cheaper; the full history stays in the transcript. Projects can set their own value in Project Settings, and the Assistant has its own (Settings → Assistant). Compact is always available once the agent has finished.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.desc: Ask before stopping a running session.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.tip: Stopped sessions can always be resumed.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.title: Confirm before stopping
settings.sessions.defaultView.desc: How the Session tab shows a project's agents until you choose with its Panes | Tiles toggle.
settings.sessions.defaultView.tip: Panes shows each agent's terminal; Tiles shows each agent as a small tile, so a whole team fits on one screen. A project remembers its own choice once you use its toggle, so changing this only affects projects that haven't chosen yet.
settings.sessions.defaultView.title: Default session view
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.desc: The Sessions tab shows new messages of a running session as they arrive.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.tip: Off: the transcript shows what was there when you opened it; Refresh loads what is new. You can also switch following on in the viewer itself. The Session tab always shows the agent working.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.titl: Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.desc: How the Overview and the session lists update while agents work.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.tip: Live updates as sessions change, at most every 15 seconds and only while the tab is shown. Each update reads the project's session files, so with many sessions or agents a slower choice keeps Combwork lighter. Refresh always updates at once.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.title: Overview updates
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.desc: Count what Combwork's Agent API, tools, guidance and skills cost, for the Performance view.
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.tip: Only totals are kept: request and reply sizes, times and outcomes, the size of what each session was given, and the providers' own reported usage. Never prompts, replies, tokens or paths. Kept 30 days per workspace in .combwork/metrics (git-ignored, this machine's). Turned off, nothing new is recorded; what was recorded stays until you reset it.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.desc: Clear this workspace's recorded performance metrics.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.tip: Starts the history again from now. Session usage and transcripts are not affected.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.title: Reset performance metrics
settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC: When Combwork closed without quitting (a crash, or it was ended), resume the agents that were running when it starts again.
Off: Combwork only tells you, with Resume All for you to choose. Either way the notice says when Combwork was last seen and which agents were running.
Resume agents after an unexpected close
settings.sessions.tileOrder.desc: The order of the agents' tiles in the Tiles view.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.tip: Same as panes keeps the agents in their panes' order, so a builder stays beside its reviewer: tiles waiting for you or stalled are highlighted where they are, and a page button counts them on other pages. By urgency puts them first, then the agents working, then the idle ones.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.title: Tile order
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.desc: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript turns orange in its footer and Combwork notifies you once.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.tip: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Combwork: each turn, resume and transcript view has more to read. Compacting doesn't shrink the file, which keeps the whole history; handing the work over to a new conversation does (click the size in the footer for Hand Over to…, and choose the agent itself). Projects can set their own value in Project Settings.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.title: Warn when a transcript is over
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.desc: Forget what the cache holds; a transcript it had is read again when it is next needed. The usage history stays.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.tip: Only needed if a running session's token counts look wrong. Nothing else is lost: sessions, transcripts, backups and the usage history stay as they are.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.title: Clear the usage cache
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.desc: How many transcripts Combwork keeps the token use of in memory while it runs, so a running session's figures follow each turn without reading it again.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.tip: What each session used is kept in the usage history, in the workspace's .combwork folder: this cache only spares reading a transcript again while Combwork runs. The least recently used go first when it is full. {min, number} to {max, number}.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.title: Usage cache size
settings.slotCopy.desc: Git-ignored files copied from the project folder into each new slot and review copy, comma separated or one per line, such as .env files. Projects inherit it, and can set their own in Version Control → Slots and copies.
settings.slotCopy.title: Files copied into new slots
settings.token.regenerateMessage: Programs using the current token will stop working. Running sessions pick up the new token when restarted.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.desc: Look for a new version of Combwork shortly after it starts and every 6 hours.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.tip: When off, Combwork only checks when you choose Help → Check for Updates…; development builds never update.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.d: Download a new version in the background as soon as it is found.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.t: When off, the status bar says a new version is available and you choose when to download it. Downloads are checked against the release checksum.
settings.updates.install.desc: When a downloaded update is installed.
settings.updates.install.tip: Automatically: the update installs when you next quit Combwork (never while it is running, so your sessions are not interrupted); Restart and Update installs it straight away. Manually: it installs only when you choose Restart and Update. Either way, Combwork asks before stopping agents that are working.
settings.updates.install.title: Install updates
settings.updates.prerelease.desc: Also offer beta versions published before a full release.
settings.updates.prerelease.tip: Pre-releases get new features first and may have rough edges. Turning this off again waits for the next full release rather than going back.
settings.updates.prerelease.title: Include pre-releases
settings.updates.status.tip: The version you are running and the result of the last check.
settings.updates.status.title: Combwork version
settings.usageCache.clearFailed: Could not clear the usage cache
settings.usageCache.clearedDetail: Each transcript is read again the next time it is shown.
settings.viewers.madeDetail: Copy it into the app it is for.
settings.viewers.makeFailed: Could not make the viewer token
settings.viewers.name: Name
settings.viewers.revokeFailed: Could not revoke the viewer token
settings.viewers.revokeMessage: The app using it can no longer read Combwork, and its event stream ends now.
settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.desc: For every workspace: what each project starts from unless its workspace or the project sets its own. Pick a preset, or set each option, for None or for Git.
settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.tip: Until 1.0’s settings tidy, Settings → Workflow defaults: nothing set there changed.
settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.title: Combwork defaults
settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.desc: For this workspace’s projects, over Combwork defaults; a project sets its own in its Version Control tab.
settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.tip: Until 1.0’s settings tidy, the workflow defaults in Settings → Workspace: nothing set there changed.
settings.workspace.antivirus.desc: Whether Microsoft Defender scans the workspace's folders as Combwork's work changes them (builds, tests, git, worktrees), and the exclusions Combwork can add for them, with your consent.
settings.workspace.antivirus.tip: Combwork checks without administrator rights, so Defender may not show its exclusions (unknown). Adding or removing exclusions asks for administrator rights once. Combwork only ever offers these folders: the workspace, its worktrees folder once it exists, and its test area for people developing Combwork. It never changes other antivirus products.
settings.workspace.antivirus.title: Antivirus scanning
settings.workspace.commands.desc: This workspace's own commands: run one by hand (here, or Run Command in the command palette), or pick it, or one of Combwork's, for when this workspace opens or closes.
settings.workspace.commands.tip: Saved in the workspace's .combwork/workspace.json, which Combwork keeps out of version control. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.workspace.commands.title: Commands
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.desc: Restore one to bring it back with its cards (and, for a removed one, the handovers packed into its folder). A folder that has left the workspace can be forgotten.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.tip: Project → Remove Project… hides a project, removes it from Combwork (its folder keeps its handovers and cards in .combwork/removed, so it can move to another workspace) or deletes it (to the Recycle Bin). Deleted projects are not listed here: restore the folder from the Recycle Bin and Combwork sees it as a new project.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.title: Hidden and removed projects
settings.workspace.onClose.desc: The commands Combwork runs, in order, as this workspace closes: its window closes, another workspace opens in it, or Combwork quits. Combwork waits for them, showing them running.
settings.workspace.onClose.tip: Pick them from Commands above. '{workspace}' becomes the workspace's folder, '{name}' its name and '{reason}' why it closes: window, switch, quit, or update when Combwork restarts to install an update (only with that box ticked). Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.workspace.onClose.title: When this workspace closes, run
settings.workspace.onOpen.desc: The commands Combwork runs, in order, as this workspace opens: a local server or a database its agents need, say. Its agents start once they're done, or once you choose Don't wait.
settings.workspace.onOpen.tip: Pick them from Commands above. '{reason}' becomes open. If one fails, Combwork asks: Rerun, Skip it and continue, or Stop here; a command ticked "The commands after this need it" leads with Stop here. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.workspace.onOpen.title: When this workspace opens, run
settings.workspace.storage.desc: What Combwork keeps for each of the workspace's projects (the biggest first) and the Assistant: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and worktrees. Storage opens a project's page, with Clean Up… and Purge…; Purge… here removes everything Combwork keeps for the sessions of the whole workspace.
settings.workspace.storage.tip: Measured in the background, a project at a time. The coding agents' own transcripts (in ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot) aren't counted. Hidden projects aren't included.
settings.workspace.storage.title: Storage
